items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation up front
Never asked about stairs or floors at either the Houston origin or the Austin apartment
Never asked about access at the destination — this is an apartment on Red River Street in downtown Austin, so elevator, loading zone, parking and COI questions are material and all went unasked
Never asked whether they need packing services
Never explained a confirmation email — only a text with the walkthrough link, so the customer leaves with no written record of the $768 trip fee and $240 hotel fee he just quoted
No bolded detail list / 'reply with corrections' handoff
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
No business hours or how-to-reach-us given
Used the customer's name once ('Am I speaking with Craig?') — needs 3+; used 'sir' and 'boss man' instead
No insurance or No Worries Damage Coverage mention at all on a two-day interstate move with an overnight truck stay
No budget-conscious framing — dropped $768 + $240 in fees flat with no cushioning or value context
Efficiency — the customer had to ask the same clock question four separate times before it landed
top_strength: He owned the hardest part of an interstate move — the two-day clock — and stayed patient through four rounds of the same question, landing a clear model: clock starts on arrival day one, pauses at the hotel, restarts when the truck leaves the hotel day two, and the trip fee is separate because it covers the empty return leg. He also closed a same-day virtual walkthrough at 3:45 and personally owns it, which is the right outcome for a 3-bedroom plus 150-box storage job.
coaching_note: Sections 3-6 were granted full N/A credit because the call legitimately routed to a virtual walkthrough before any hourly rate or estimate was delivered — the fees quoted were direct answers to the customer's own questions. The real fix: even on a scheduler call, send a written confirmation of what was discussed and always ask destination access questions — this is a downtown Austin apartment and elevator/loading-zone/COI issues are the most likely thing to blow up a two-day interstate estimate.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and genuinely patient — 'no worries', 'I'll be happy to explain it for you', and the 'I started as a mover myself, you're in good hands' line clearly landed with the customer ('you do it all man'), though heavy filler ('cool cool cool', 'alrighty') keeps it short of Outstanding.
